usageNotes: Creates a SPICE shell session on a specific node, returning connection parameters (host, tls-port, password, proxy, type) that can be passed directly to the 'remote-viewer' application for an interactive terminal. Requires the 'Sys.Console' privilege on '/nodes/{node}'; commands other than 'login' (e.g., 'upgrade', 'ceph_install') additionally require 'root@pam' authentication. Specify the 'proxy' parameter as the hostname used to reach the API so SPICE traffic is routed through a reachable node.

examples.summary: Open a SPICE login shell on node pve1, routing through the same node as SPICE proxy

tips: Pass the returned object directly to 'remote-viewer' (e.g., via a .vv connection file) — the password is single-use and short-lived.
The 'proxy' field defaults to the node running the request; set it explicitly to whatever hostname your client can actually reach to avoid SPICE connection failures in multi-node clusters.
The 'cmd-opts' field accepts null-terminated strings for passing extra arguments to built-in commands like 'upgrade' or 'ceph_install'.
SPICE requires the 'spiceproxy' service to be running on the target node (enabled by default on PVE nodes).
